clue.text: In the piano section an organ is used

indicators.note: the word in tells the solver to look within the following words for a run of letters

explanation.surface: A musician notes that an organ is being played in the piano section of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals a run of letters inside 'piano section'. The 'organ' is a body part, not the musical instrument the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is the smelling organ of the face.

clue.text: Denizen of the deep the opposite of a dingy colour, on one part of bank

indicators.note: the opposite of here means the colour word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
I is the Roman numeral one
a branch is a local office of a bank

explanation.surface: A sea creature, far from dull in colour, sits on a section of a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opposite of' turns DUN into NUD. The 'bank' is a financial one, not a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudibranch is a sea slug, often brightly coloured, living on the seabed.

clue.text: Start talking in his trial about a flap

indicators.note: in says the opening letter goes inside the rearranged letters
about says the letters of his trial are moved round into a new order
start says only the opening letter of talking is used

explanation.surface: A defendant begins speaking at his trial about a moment of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' gives T from 'talking'; 'about' rearranges HIS TRIAL, and 'in' puts T among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt-tail is the loose flap at the bottom of a shirt.

clue.text: An unfinished weapon put among the skilful is hateful

parts.note: an becomes the single letter A

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its final letter, so the last letter of the weapon word goes

parts.note: a bomb is a weapon
among here gives the little word in
skilful people are able

explanation.surface: Putting a half-made weapon among capable people is a detestable act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last B from BOMB, leaving BOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abominable is detestable, deserving loathing.

clue.text: Fellow about fifty is a deceiver

indicators.note: about says the word for fellow goes round the letter for fifty

parts.note: a buffer is an old fellow, often an old buffer
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A man of about fifty turns out to be a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an approximation of age but puts BUFFER around L. A buffer is British slang for a fusty old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluffer pretends to more than they have, as in poker.

clue.text: Me holding a part of the fork for the entertainment

indicators.note: holding says the word me wraps round the fork part

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: Someone grips a fork prong ready for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals a container; 'the entertainment' is a theatre show, not something one does with a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance at a theatre or cinema.

clue.text: Toy weapons which could give one a break

definitions.meaning: playthings for a nursery, guns a child might play with

definitions.text: which could give one a break
definitions.meaning: in billiards, a series of gentle close shots building a scoring run, or break

explanation.surface: Toy guns that might give someone a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards a break is a scoring run, and a cannon is a shot striking both other balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase names children's toy guns; in billiards it names small repeated shots that build a scoring run.

clue.text: Begin changing for a party

indicators.note: changing says the letters of begin take a new order

explanation.surface: A party is about to start with a change of plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spree of drinking or eating, a wild party.

clue.text: Woman right for always

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, a common female name

explanation.surface: A woman is right forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, for good.

clue.text: Bury a relative when they rely on each other

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a dependent is a family member supported by another

explanation.surface: A family buries a relative, each leaning on the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Things are mutually reliant when each needs the other, which the adjective describes; 'when' links.

clue.text: Condescend to provide a plan with the south missing

indicators.note: missing says the letter for south is absent from the plan word

parts.note: a design is a plan
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to drawing up a plan, leaving out the southern part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes S out of DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one thinks beneath oneself.

clue.text: Expression of an extreme article by the Church

parts.note: utter means complete or extreme
an is the indefinite article
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman voices an extreme article of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something spoken, a verbal expression.

clue.text: They are prone to let things slip but greet friend awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of the preceding words are put together clumsily, in a new order

explanation.surface: Clumsy people drop things but welcome a friend in an ungainly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges BUT GREET FRIEND. 'They are' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter-fingered person is clumsy and drops whatever they hold, as if their hands were greasy.

clue.text: Perhaps it takes a gent in his prime to ensure conception

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man in his prime is needed to father a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges A GENT and PRIME; 'it takes' and 'in his' tie the picture together.
explanation.definitionFit: To impregnate is to make pregnant, causing conception.

clue.text: Prize-giver who is the one in charge of prisoners

parts.note: one becomes the letter A, as in a single thing
a warder guards prisoners in a jail

explanation.surface: A prison officer is also the person handing out the prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who confers an award is the one handing out a prize.

clue.text: The delightful place is all around ane beside the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: around says the word for all goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a sum is a total, everything added together
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lovely place encircles one and sits next to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'ane' is a misreading of 'one'. 'around' signals the container; Ely is a small English cathedral city in the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the paradise of Greek myth, so any blissful spot.

clue.text: Complicated one in church with a fashionable gallery about

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: about says the gallery name goes round the church letters

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside the church letters

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for the Roman Catholic church
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a church with a stylish gallery around it finds it all baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'about' signal two nested containers. The Tate is the London gallery; RC stands for Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means full of detail, elaborate and complex.

clue.text: Plays badly in company for a song

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the company abbreviation
badly says the word plays is mangled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone performs poorly in a group and is given a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' and 'in' signal anagram and container; 'Plays' reads as a verb but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of song, with roots in Trinidad.

clue.text: Outside broadcasting is free from building

parts.note: outside, as in out in the open
on air means broadcasting

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast is made free of any studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcasting' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-air happens outdoors, not under a roof.

clue.text: Waste skill looking back about one for a criminal

indicators.note: about says the reversed letters go round the letter for one
looking back says the two words before it are read from right to left

parts.note: rot is decay or waste
art is skill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Squandered talent, seen in hindsight, makes someone a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' reverses both pieces together and 'about' slots the one inside, between the two reversed words.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor commits treason, a serious crime against their country.

clue.text: Watch expert has to go quietly in a strange motion

indicators.note: in says the soft letter goes inside the rearranged letters
strange says the letters of motion are made odd, in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A clock expert must slip away silently during an odd movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns MOTION into TOMION; 'in' puts P inside. Thomas Tompion was a famous 17th-century English watchmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tompion was a celebrated English clockmaker, called the father of English watchmaking.

clue.text: Damn reign spoilt by nobleman giving opposite instructions

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

indicators.note: spoilt says the letters of the two words are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman curses a reign that has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges the letters of 'Damn reign'; 'by' merely joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Countermanding means revoking an order by issuing a contrary one.

clue.text: Colouring matter used for decoration in a mineral

indicators.note: in says the decoration letters sit inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a mineral that is mined
CH, Companion of Honour, a British decoration

explanation.surface: A pigment used for ornament is found in a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoration' looks like the pigment's use but is CH, the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment, yellow to brown, used since prehistoric times.

clue.text: Beat up own side

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to slap is to beat

explanation.surface: Someone beats up members of their own team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SLAP into PALS, reading upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Your pals are your friends, the people on your side.

clue.text: King is held by a female and Hitler's follower is a Jew

indicators.note: is held by says the king letter is gripped inside the phrase for a female

parts.note: a she is a female
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
a Nazi was a member of Hitler's party

explanation.surface: An awkward clue linking a woman holding a monarch to a Nazi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is held by' puts K inside A SHE, giving ASHKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashkenazim are Jews of Central and Eastern European descent.

clue.text: Lake in which many a sailor sets sail

indicators.note: in which points the solver to letters lodged inside the following words

explanation.surface: A lake where plenty of sailors set off on voyages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' signals letters inside 'many a sailor'; 'sets sail' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa, now usually called Lake Malawi, is a large African lake.

clue.text: Strange singer holds German world to be extremely hot

indicators.note: holds says the rearranged letters enclose the German word
strange says the letters of singer are made odd, in a new order

parts.note: Welt is German for world

explanation.surface: An odd vocalist clutches a German globe and feels the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the singer and 'holds' wraps those letters round the German word, just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweltering means oppressively hot, the kind of heat that makes one sweat.

clue.text: Celebrate, but it sounds like doom

indicators.note: it sounds like says the word for doom is heard, not spelt, in the grid

parts.note: fate is doom or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone would celebrate, but the word rings of grim destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them with festivities.
